action.mutates: sends one RFC3164 line (host p8testremote, tag p8test) to 127.0.0.1:6514 over TLS with the node's own Puppet certificate as the client certificate; rsyslogd creates /var/log/hosts/p8testremote/p8test.log and, through the stock /etc/rsyslog.d/50-default.conf (the listener's rules do not stop the message), appends the same line to /var/log/syslog

creates a throwaway RSA key and self-signed certificate (CN p8test-selfsigned) in /run/p8test-rsyslog; sends one RFC3164 line (host p8testremote, tag p8test) to 127.0.0.1:6514 over TLS with it; rsyslogd logs the refused session to syslog (the journal, /var/log/syslog, and through the listener's own rules the node's /var/log/hosts/<node>/rsyslogd.log)

runs `logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/rsyslog-hosts` once (it renames the per-host logs, HUPs rsyslog and updates logrotate's state file /var/lib/logrotate/status); sends one more RFC3164 line over TLS with the node's own certificate; rsyslogd creates a new /var/log/hosts/p8testremote/p8test.log and appends to /var/log/syslog

creates /var/log/hosts/p8testold with p8test.log-<10 days ago> and p8test.log-<2 days ago> (clear text) and older.log-20200101.gz (mtime 10 days ago) and newer.log-20200102.gz (mtime 2 days ago); runs the retention script once as root (it gzips, touches and deletes in /var/log/hosts)

outcomes.outcome: rsyslogd listens on the port over TLS with the node's own certificate, configured for the per-host tree and the session limit
a message from a client with a CA-signed certificate lands in <log_root>/hosts/<hostname>/<program>.log; a client with a self-signed certificate is refused
the per-host logs rotate daily at the rotation time, date-suffixed and uncompressed, and rsyslog reopens its files after the rotation
rotated logs older than the active period are compressed and compressed logs older than the retention period are deleted, from root's cron at the retention time
